messages.subject: regular expressions in R and diacritics
messages.subject_clean: regular expressions in R and diacritics
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

 

This is a bit unusual question, but hopefully still topical on doing language science with R.

 

I am working on a corpus of written Maltese, most of which comes from online sources,

such as newspaper comments and alike. And hence I  have to deal with things
like commenters using all kind of non-text symbols.

(an example: Ha ha ha ha ha Ha ha ha ha ha!!!!! Are you serious??????Tajba din!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!)

 

I want to split the different comments into words and found the regular expression

“\W+” super useful (at first sight). This means “split by anything which is not a letter”, thereby only getting the words.

This works perfectly on examples such as the one above, getting the words

 

Ha-ha…etc.-Are-you-serious-Tajba-din

 

However, it turns out that what is considered a “word” is surprisingly Anglocentric. 

 

A phrase such as

“… jkun kapaċi jħares “

Is parsed into the “words”

jkun – kapaÄ – i – jÄ – ares

 

As you can see, the letters with diacritics lead to problems, with the words being split.

 

This probably is due to the fact that “internally” these UTF8 encoded characters with diacritics are treated as two characters,

With the first being Ä and the second not recognized as a letter by the \w character set. Does anybody have an idea how to solve this,
that is, influence that the character class \w (and hence is negation \W) accepts diacritics as part of words?

 

Thanks in advance for any pointers,

Holger

messages.body_plain:
Hi Holger,

Would you mind including an example that generates the error?  I did this
and (I think) got the result you expect:

library(stringr)
s <- "… jkun kapaċi jħares"
str_split(string = s, pattern = boundary("word"))
[[1]]
[1] "jkun"   "kapaċi" "jħares"

Alex

Hi Holger,

I can’t replicate this behavior:

> gsub('\\W+', '-', 'jkun kapaċi jħares')
[1] "jkun-kapaċi-jħares“

Do you perhaps not have your session set to UTF8?

Best
James

messages.body_plain:
Maybe using Unicode categories like this can help?

strsplit(
   "… jkun kapaċi jħares ",
   "[^\\p{L}]+",
   perl=TRUE)

(See <https://www.regular-expressions.info/refunicode.html>)

HTH,
STG
--
